'''''Viola reichenbachiana''''', also known as the '''early dog-violet''', '''pale wood violet''', '''slender wood violet''', '''hedge violet''', or '''wood dog violet''', is a species of flowering plant in the ''Viola'' genus.<ref name="NatureGate">{{Cite web |title=Early Dog Violet, Viola reichenbachiana - Flowers - NatureGate |url=https://luontoportti.com/en/t/2352/early-dog-violet |access-date=2024-04-09 |website=luontoportti.com}}</ref><ref>''Viola reichenbachiana'' Jord. ex Boreau in GBIF Secretariat (2022). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset {{doi|10.15468/39omei}} accessed via GBIF.org</ref><ref name="Candide">“Early Dog Violet (Viola Reichenbachiana) - Plants.” ''Candide'', https://candide.com/IE/plants/df534849-458c-4122-98bc-31d13f2f5891 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528163647/https://candide.com/IE/plants/df534849-458c-4122-98bc-31d13f2f5891 |date=2022-05-28 }}.</ref><ref name="Ganeshaiah">“Viola Reichenbachiana Jordan Ex Boreau: Species.” Ganeshaiah, K. N., UAS, Bangalore, India.; Kailash, B. R., ATREE, Bangalore, India.; Royal Norwegian Embassy grants. Indian Bioresource Information Network (IBIN), Department of Biotechnology, New Delhi, India. ''India Biodiversity Portal'', IBP, https://indiabiodiversity.org/species/show/262252.</ref> This species [[Hybrid plant|hybridises]] with ''[[Viola riviniana]]'', the common dog-violet, to produce ''Viola'' × ''bavarica''.<ref>{{cite book | last=Stace | first=Clive A. | title=New flora of the British Isles | publisher=Cambridge University Press | publication-place=Cambridge | date=2010 | isbn=978-0-521-70772-5 | oclc=647075102 | author-link=Clive A. Stace}}</ref> The plant is named after the 19th-century botanist [[Ludwig Reichenbach]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Boreau |first=A. |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/44735 |title=Flore du centre de la France et du bassin de la Loire, ou, Description des plantes qui croissent spontanément, ou qui sont cultivées en grand dans les départements arrosés par la Loire et ses affluents, avec l'analyse des genres et des espèces |last2=Boreau |first2=A. |date=1857 |publisher=Librairie encyclopédique de Roret |edition=3e éd., très augm. |volume=1857. |location=Paris}}</ref> It is a rhizomatous [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] that is widely known for its purple petals, and it typically resides along road banks or among other rich vegetation, as other wild pansies do.<ref name="NatureGate" /><ref name="FirstNature-2022">“Viola Reichenbachiana - Early Dog-Violet.” ''FirstNature'', 2022, https://www.first-nature.com/flowers/viola-reichenbachiana.php.</ref> The name dog violet refers to its lack of scent, making it supposedly only fit for dogs.<ref>“Viola Riviniana - Common Dog-Violet.” ''FirstNature'', 2022, https://www.first-nature.com/flowers/viola-riviniana.php#:~:text=Common%20Dog-violets%20%28referred%20to%20as%20Dog-violets%20because%20they,as%20late%20as%20the%20start%20of%20July.%20Uses.</ref><ref name="Candide" />

== Description ==
''Viola reichenbachiana'' grows to {{cvt|5-15|cm|in|abbr=on}} in height and {{cvt|10-50|cm|in|abbr=on}} in spread.<ref name="Candide" /> The leaf orientation is simple and grows alternately.<ref name="NatureGate" /><ref name="Ganeshaiah" /> The plant has wide, heart-shaped blades with rounded, tooth-like ridges.<ref name="NatureGate" /><ref name="Candide" /><ref name="FirstNature-2022" /> The leaves may be hairless or very slightly textured, and their tips may be pointed or hooked.<ref name="Candide" /><ref name="FirstNature-2022" /> Its upper leaves tend to be smaller and darker in color.<ref name="Ganeshaiah" /> Its leaf typically has 4 or 5 veins on either side of a main vein called the midrib.<ref name="Ganeshaiah" />

The flower of ''Viola reichenbachiana'' is bisexual, containing both male and female reproductive structures.<ref name="Ganeshaiah" /> It has 3 or 5 narrow, non-overlapping petals that are a signature dull purple.<ref name="NatureGate" /><ref name="Ganeshaiah" /> The flower typically has 5 small, pointed sepals, 5 stamens, and 1 carpel.<ref name="NatureGate" /> These flowers can range from 1.5 to 2 cm across.<ref name="Ganeshaiah" /> They can be recognized by their star-like appearance due to the separated petals or their deep violet-blue spurs.<ref name="Candide" /><ref name="RHS Gardening">“Viola Reichenbachiana - RHS Gardening.” ''RHS Plant Finder & Selector'', Royal Horticultural Society, https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/98441/viola-reichenbachiana/details.</ref> Pollination can occur via insects, self-pollination, or cross-pollination.<ref name="Ganeshaiah" />

Its seeds have rather thick cotyledons to nourish the embryo, and the fruits that develop around them usually have 3 lobes.<ref name="NatureGate" /> The roots have many root hairs for absorption and grow rhizomatously, meaning they propagate through above-ground runners known as stolons.<ref name="Candide" /><ref name="FirstNature-2022" />

== Cultivation ==
''Viola reichenbachiana'' is found throughout central Europe spanning all the way to parts of Asia around the Himalayan Mountains.<ref name="FirstNature-2022" /> It resides in regions such as England, Scotland, Wales, North Africa, China, India, and Pakistan.<ref name="FirstNature-2022" /> Its natural habitats include hardwood forests or other wooded areas with broad leaves.<ref name="NatureGate" /> It grows most successfully under maximum or partial sunlight and moderate watering, and the minimum temperature at which it can survive is -20 degrees Celsius.<ref name="Candide" /><ref name="RHS Gardening" /> It thrives in acidic to neutral fertile soil that is damp but well-drained.<ref name="RHS Gardening" /><ref>“Viola Reichenbachiana - Jordan.” ''Plants for a Future Database'', PFAF, https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Viola%2Breichenbachiana#:~:text=The%20plant%20is%20used%20as,sores%20and%20wounds%5B240%5D.</ref> They normally take approximately 3 years to reach maturity, and are grown mainly for the aesthetic of their distinct flowers.<ref name="Candide" /> Its flowers typically bloom between late February and May, and its fruits are produced from May to August.<ref name="FirstNature-2022" />

The plant faces predation by slugs, snails, red spider mites, gall midges, and aphids, and it is also the food source for fritillary butterfly larvae.<ref name="Candide" /><ref name="FirstNature-2022" /><ref name="RHS Gardening" /><ref name="Oldhouseweb-2022">“Viola Diseases.” ''Old House Web'', OHW Database, 2022, https://www.oldhouseweb.com/gardening/viola-diseases.shtml.</ref> Common diseases include the browning of petals and leaves due to anthracnose fungus, powdery mildew, stem rot, rust on leaf undersides, and smut pustules on leaf stalks that discharge spores.<ref name="Ganeshaiah" /><ref name="Oldhouseweb-2022" />

=== RHS Hardiness ===
The Royal Horticultural Society recognizes ''V. reichenbachiana'' as an H6 on the Hardiness Scale, meaning that it is "hardy in all of UK and northern Europe", and its minimum temperature ranges are -20 to -15 degrees Celsius.<ref name="RHS Gardening" />
